page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.1-4 is a compute-oriented virtual machine instance featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. It provides 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with hyper-threading enabled on an Intel Xeon 6354 processor operating at 3.0 GHz. The configuration includes 4.0 GB of system memory, alongside 32 KB L1 data cache, 4 MB L2 cache, and 16 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector instruction extensions including AVX, AVX-512 Foundation, and AVX-512 VNNI, alongside cryptographic hardware acceleration. No local disk storage or GPU hardware is bundled, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate moderate single-threaded capability counterbalanced by low total throughput dictated by the 2-vCPU constraint. The instance records mid-range results in single-core evaluations, achieving a Geekbench single-core score of 1658.0 and a stress-ng single-core score of 1883.48, supported by steady performance in single-threaded gzip compression at 28.66 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-threaded metrics rank in the bottom tiers across broader server benchmarks, reflecting a Geekbench multi-core score of 1927.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 3014.85. Memory subsystem tests indicate uncached large-block read speeds of 15.84 GB/sec and write speeds of 14.20 GB/sec, producing a weak overall PassMark memory rating of 1278.68.

From an architectural efficiency standpoint, the instance delivers predictable, dedicated compute execution for smaller workloads without shared-core interference, though the absence of onboard NVMe storage necessitates external network-attached volumes for persistent data. Workload profiles aligned with this server include lightweight compute tasks, small-scale web serving, microservices, continuous integration build agents, and single-threaded data transformation jobs.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Optimized3.Flex.1-4 is a compute-focused instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6354 processor running at 3.0 GHz on x86_64 architecture. The server allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs across 1 physical core with 4.0 GB of memory, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Cache resources include 4 MB L2 cache and 16 MB L3 cache, backed by AVX-512 and hardware cryptographic instructions. The instance provides no bundled local storage or GPU accelerators, but includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. Benchmarks exhibit average single-core execution with a Geekbench score of 1658.0 and gzip compression at 28.66 GB/sec, whereas aggregate multi-threaded metrics remain modest due to the minimal core count. Without onboard NVMe disks, storage depends entirely on remote volumes. This profile is appropriate for lightweight microservices, single-threaded processing pipelines, utility scripts, and low-traffic web applications.
